title: Matching open orders to idle drivers
name: Driver dispatch board

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how DispatchBoard.assign() acquires and releases its lock across all the paths through the method? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
assign() scans every idle driver while holding the lock. What does this imply as the number of idle drivers grows?
choices: Assignments run in parallel, because each worker scans its own copy of the driver map.
The time the lock is held, and so the delay for every other operation, grows in proportion to the number of idle drivers.
The scan is safe because HashMap iteration is thread-safe.
Late drivers are skipped because values() is a snapshot taken before the loop.

questions.prompt: Two requests call submit() with the same order id but different details before any driver is assigned. What is on the board afterwards?
choices: Both orders, under the same id.
An exception is thrown for the second call.
The first order, because put() ignores existing keys.
Only the later order; the earlier one is replaced.

questions.prompt: A monitoring endpoint calls stats() while dispatch workers are busy. How does it behave if the lock is held for longer than 50 ms?
choices: It blocks until the lock is released, so the endpoint can hang.
It reads the maps without the lock and may return slightly stale numbers.
It returns Optional.empty() and does not wait further.
It interrupts the thread that holds the lock.
